description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary Director, Services Technology Risk Who is Mastercard? Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential. Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all. Overview: The Services Technology Risk team is looking for a Director, Service Technology Risk professional to help maintain secure, resilient, and trusted technology environments while enabling innovation and growth. The ideal candidate is analytical, collaborative, and proactive, with a passion for identifying and managing risks, strengthening controls, and partnering with Engineering, Product, Security, and Business teams. This role will focus on improving risk management and assurance practices through automation, analytics, and scalable solutions while supporting regulatory, audit, and customer expectations. Role: The Director, Services Technology Risk will lead the identification, assessment, prioritization, monitoring, and escalation of technology and operational risks across Services. This role will develop risk management strategies and frameworks, including risk registers, product risk assessments, and risk and control self-assessments, providing leadership with clear insights to support informed decisions. The role will partner with Product, Engineering, and Security teams to embed risk management into business and technology processes, strengthen accountability, and ensure risks are effectively managed. The ideal candidate brings deep technology risk expertise, strong business judgment, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, translate complex risks into business impact, and build scalable capabilities that support secure innovation and growth. title: Technical Accounting Policy Manager
description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At  Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.”  learn more about working at Coinbase . Coinbase is looking for a Technical Accounting Policy Manager to join the Accounting team. This highly visible individual contributor role sits at the intersection of Technical Accounting Policy, Controllership, and strategic business initiatives. You’ll shape how Coinbase accounts for new and evolving crypto products, complex transactions, and emerging accounting matters while partnering across Finance, Legal, Tax, Product, and external advisors. Reporting to the Director of Reporting and Technical Accounting Policy, you’ll help translate complex business developments into clear, well-supported accounting conclusions. This is a remote role. What You’ll Do Shape Coinbase’s accounting policies for new products and complex transactions; write technical accounting memos and bring conclusions to closure with external auditors. Monitor emerging accounting guidance and business developments, assess their impact on Coinbase, and recommend practical, risk-aware accounting conclusions. Lead accounting analyses for strategic investments and other complex transactions under ASC 321, ASC 323, and ASC 810, including equity-method, fair-value, and consolidation considerations. Support M&A and other strategic transactions by coordinating accounting diligence, evaluating deal terms, and advising on purchase accounting under ASC 805 when applicable. Deliver original footnote, MD&A, and transaction-related disclosures for 10-Q and 10-K filings, and help ensure related SOX controls are designed and operating effectively. Partner with Corporate Development, Legal, Tax, FP&A, Product, and Controllership to support new product launches, strategic initiatives, and post-close integration activities. Manage external advisors as needed, including scoping engagements, reviewing deliverables, and maintaining quality and timeline accountability. Required Skills and Experience 9+ years of progressive accounting experience, including experience in public accounting and industry; CPA required. Big 4 experience is strongly preferred. Strong US GAAP knowledge, including direct experience with technical accounting, investment accounting, consolidation, and business combinations. Experience analyzing complex transactions and translating business arrangements into clear accounting conclusions. Experience drafting technical accounting memos and original financial statement disclosures, and communicating complex conclusions clearly to cross-functional stakeholders. Experience managing external consultants or advisors and holding them to clear quality and timeline standards. Strong judgment, organization, and ability to manage competing reporting, policy, and strategic initiative deadlines in an evolving business. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.   Position ID: P77060 #LI-Remote Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). title: Senior Product Manager
description: Bloomreach is building the world’s premier  agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the  entire  customer journey. We're taking  autonomous search  mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses. We’re making  conversational shopping  a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey. We're designing the future of  autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do. And we're building all of that on the intelligence of a single AI engine —  Loomi — so that personalization isn't only autonomous…it's also consistent.From retail to financial services, hospitality to gaming, businesses use Bloomreach to drive higher growth and lasting loyalty. We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.  We are looking for a Senior AI Product manager to join the Bloomreach Clarity product team and help build the next generation of conversational shopping . Working in one of our Central European offices or from home on a full time basis, you’ll become a core part of the Product Team, and report to the head of product for Clarity.  Clarity is an exciting rapidly growing product in an emerging market opportunity, built on the latest in LLM technology. This is an amazing opportunity to be at the frontier of AI-native product development, and to build a product that sets the bar for the next generation of commerce interfaces. We operate in a rapidly evolving landscape and value an entrepreneurial mindset, rapid iteration, sharp thinking, curiosity, and a laser focus on outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Drive the development of new AI-native capabilities within Clarity, from ideation through to launch, with a focus on unlocking real business value. Collaborate closely with engineers, designers, and product leaders to rapidly prototype and iterate on features powered by Generative AI and LLMs . Engage deeply with customers to understand their evolving needs in the AI space and translate those into innovative, intelligent product solutions. Partner with Customer Success and Data teams to ensure successful rollout of new AI driven features, streamlining workflows and gathering both qualitative and quantitative feedback. Stay on the pulse of AI and GenAI advancements , market trends, and competitive offerings, translating insights into strategic bets and product direction. Set the gold standard for how AI features are delivered, ensuring strong user adoption, ethical implementation, and customer satisfaction. Monitor and report on AI product usage, performance, and business impact using a data-first approach, ensuring every decision is backed by insight. Regularly synthesize findings and communicate progress, opportunities, and outcomes to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. Personal Attributes: A product first, AI curious mindset , driven by impact and always looking for ways to push boundaries. Deep empathy for users and a data informed, experimental approach to solving real world problems with emerging tech. A natural collaborator who thrives in high autonomy environments and loves owning outcomes. Crystal clear communicator able to make complex AI and product decisions understandable to stakeholders across the business. Grit, creativity, and a constant drive to learn, especially in fast evolving fields like GenAI. Professional Experience: 3–6+ years in B2B SaaS Product Management , with experience in high growth, innovative product environments. Proven success delivering AI powered or GenAI driven features , or a strong demonstrable interest and understanding of how LLMs, embeddings, and conversational interfaces drive product value. Hands on involvement in product led growth initiatives and scaling usage of intelligent product experiences. Demonstrated comfort working with engineers, data scientists, and researchers in cross functional, global teams. Familiarity with ethical considerations and responsible AI implementation is a strong plus. #LI-HO1 The pay range actually offered will take into account a variety of potential factors considered in compensation, including but not limited to skills, qualifications, geographic location, accomplishments, experience, credentials, internal equity and business needs, and may vary from the range listed above. Base Salary Range €41.905 — €52.381 EUR More things you'll like about Bloomreach: Culture: A great deal of freedom and trust. At Bloomreach we don’t clock in and out, and we have neither corporate rules nor long approval processes. This freedom goes hand in hand with responsibility.

title: Director, Litigation and Regulatory
description: About Sezzle: With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role:  Sezzle is a publicly traded consumer finance company (Nasdaq: SEZL) building purchase-now-pay-later products for consumers who are underserved by traditional credit, and we are pursuing a de novo national bank charter. That combination puts us in front of regulators, plaintiffs' counsel, and state enforcement authorities more often than a company our size would normally be, and we handle almost all of it in-house.  This role is for a lawyer who wants to own that work rather than route it. You will run litigation and pre-litigation disputes, manage regulatory inquiries and investigations from federal and state authorities, and serve as the legal owner of our privacy and data protection framework. You will have real autonomy on day one, direct access to the executive team, and the budget discipline of a lean function that brings in outside counsel deliberately rather than reflexively. What You'll Do: Litigation and disputes Manage consumer litigation, class actions, arbitrations, and commercial disputes from intake through resolution, including case strategy, discovery, and settlement posture. Direct outside counsel where we use it: scope, budget, staffing, and strategy. You set the plan; they execute it. Own litigation holds, ESI protocols, custodian identification, and the discovery process end to end. Manage the small-claims and arbitration pipeline, and build the process improvements that keep volume from becoming a drag. Identify the patterns behind repeat disputes and take them back to product, operations, and collections so the underlying problem gets fixed. Regulatory inquiries and investigations Manage civil investigative demands, examination requests, subpoenas, and informal inquiries from the CFPB, FTC, state attorneys general, and state financial regulators. Run productions: scope negotiation, data collection, privilege review, and delivery, working with engineering, data, and compliance. Draft response letters, white papers, and advocacy submissions, and participate directly in regulator meetings. Track the enforcement and supervisory landscape across BNPL, UDAAP, credit reporting, debt collection, and consumer disclosure, and translate it into concrete guidance for the business. Support supervisory readiness as we build toward bank charter approval and the examination posture that follows. Privacy and data protection Serve as legal owner of the privacy framework: policies, notices, records of processing, data mapping, and retention. Advise on state comprehensive privacy laws, GLBA, FCRA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, and the pixel and session-replay wiretap theories that continue to generate demand letters and class actions. Review vendor and partner data flows, negotiate data protection terms, and handle escalated consumer privacy rights requests. Partner with the Chief Compliance and Privacy Officer on incident response and on the operational privacy program. AI and how the function scales Use AI to multiply your own throughput across research, document review, discovery, production, drafting, and regulatory tracking, and keep pushing what that stack can do. Build durable tooling, not one-off prompts: skills, workflows, templates, and automations that outlive the matter they were built for and that the rest of the team can run. Champion responsible AI adoption across the company. Legal is a builder here, not a brake. You will help business teams find ways to use these tools well and help set the guardrails that make that possible. Advise on AI governance as a legal matter: model use, vendor diligence, data handling, disclosure, and the emerging regulatory picture. Advisory and cross-functional Counsel product, marketing, engineering, and collections on live questions with practical answers, not memos that end in “it depends.” Build the playbooks, templates, and internal training that let the function scale without adding headcount. What We Look For: Bachelor's degree from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction. You will need to satisfy in-house counsel

title: Sr. Director, Product Management

You’ll lead a product organization of approximately 10-15 people, setting the vision and strategy across a broad, high-impact area while developing the leaders and teams responsible for bringing that strategy to life. You’ll identify opportunities that can meaningfully expand Chime’s reach and impact, make consequential choices about where we invest, and turn those opportunities into products and experiences members love. This is a highly strategic leadership role for someone who can move fluidly between setting a multi-year vision, leading a scaled organization, and partnering with senior leaders across Chime to define what comes next. In this role, you can expect to Set a compelling product vision and strategy for a significant area of Chime, connecting member needs, market opportunities, and company priorities into a clear path forward. title: Head of Risk and Money Services
description: About Gusto At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve. All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy . AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. Head of Risk & Money Services At Gusto, we help more than 500,000 small businesses create great places to work for their people. We do this through modern payroll, employee benefits, expert HR, and financial services. We are searching for a seasoned financial services operator and regulated-domain leader to own one of Gusto's most consequential customer-facing functions: Risk & Money Services. This role sits within CX and Gusto's Financial Services organization and reports directly to the Head of Financial Services. Every dollar that moves through Gusto's platform — payroll being delivered on time, wages being deposited into Gusto Wallet, cash advances being issued, disputes being resolved — carries real financial and regulatory weight. Risk & Money Services is the team that protects this trust at the most critical edges of money movement: fraud and payment risk decisioning, Reg E dispute operations, collections, and the consumer money products that sit at the intersection of and its small business mission. This function spans three interconnected practices: Risk Operations — fraud ops, account takeover detection, payment-risk decisioning, and collections across both employer and employee money movement. This team makes real-time, high-stakes decisions on whether payroll goes out when something looks wrong, BSA/AML compliance, whether a fund recovery effort can be executed in time, and whether a fraud signal warrants action. The financial impact of individual calls is material. Focusing on risk mitigation and exceptional service is no easy task Dispute Operations — Reg E dispute processing across Gusto's banking and money-movement products, from intake through resolution and provisional credit decisioning. This team owns Gusto's most regulated customer-facing process and operates at the intersection of customer trust and regulatory obligation. Money Services and Banking — the operational home for Gusto Wallet, Cash Advance, and Gusto's expanding consumer financial products. This team is responsible for building the operational infrastructure that supports Gusto's growth in consumer banking — while protecting the customers who depend on it. You will lead this organization through a senior leadership team, who carry full ownership for their function's outcomes, not just execution within it.Partner deeply with Compliance, Legal, Engineering, and Product across Gusto's products, and serve as the operational owner of the functions that sit at the regulated edge of Gusto's financial platform This is a builder's role. Our mission is to create a world where work empowers a better life, and it starts right here at Gusto. That's why we're committed to building a collaborative and inclusive workplace, both physically and virtually. Here's what you'll do Own Risk & Money Services end to end. Own the customer experience, the regulatory posture, and the financial outcomes across this entire function. Lead a multi-disciplinary regulated financial services organization through leaders who lead. Direct an organization spanning risk operations, dispute and fraud operations, and consumer money — through leaders who own their function end to end, whom you'll continue to develop, hire, and scale. Be the keeper of quality, speed, and regulatory integrity across all three practices. Stand up Risk & Money Services as a defined operational function. Define the governance, the metrics framework, the SLAs, and the reporting infrastructure for a function that is being formalized for the first time. title: Manager, Technical & Operational Accounting
description: About the Team OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission. The Technical Accounting, Accounting Policy, and Financial Reporting organization partners across Finance to assess complex corporate matters and develop well-supported U.S. GAAP conclusions. The team supports non-routine business activities requiring thoughtful technical judgment, scalable accounting policies, financial statement disclosures, processes, and controls. About the Role You will partner closely with Technical Accounting, Financial Reporting and Controllership to translate complex accounting conclusions into scalable operational procedures. You will build processes for non-standard transactions, including warrants, equity-method investments, debt and equity securities, non-controlling interests, hypothetical liquidation at book value allocations, business combinations, and other complex financing, investment, and capital arrangements. You will advise stakeholders across Corporate Accounting, Financial Reporting, Treasury, Legal, Tax, Strategic Finance, FP&A, Equity, Internal Controls, valuation specialists, and external auditors. You will help resolve complex accounting questions, align leaders on material judgments and risks, and translate conclusions into audit-ready memoranda, close entries, disclosures, processes, and controls. This is a highly visible role for an accounting professional who can turn technical conclusions into practical execution, support non-routine transactions through recurring close processes, and strengthen operational accounting across Finance. In this role, you will: - Own operational accounting for complex financing, investment, equity, and capital arrangements, including classification, measurement, presentation, disclosure, and recurring close processes. - In partnership with technical accounting, lead day-one and recurring accounting for non-standard transactions, including fair-value measurements, equity-method investments, debt and equity securities, warrants, noncontrolling interests, and hypothetical liquidation at book value allocations. - Perform reconciliations for assigned accounts, investigate discrepancies, and drive issues to resolution. - Support the resolution of complex accounting matters during monthly and quarterly close. Ensure conclusions are reflected in financial statement presentation, footnote disclosures, journal entries, reconciliations, ownership, and controls. - Build operational processes to assess impairment indicators and asset recoverability for goodwill, intangible assets, long-lived asset groups, equity-method investments, nonmarketable equity investments, and debt securities, as applicable. - Coordinate valuations for non-standard transactions with Technical Accounting and valuation specialists. - Lead audit support for assigned investments and other complex accounting areas. Prepare evidence-backed schedules, memoranda, reconciliations, valuation support, and financial statement tie-outs. - Analyze significant equity and other compensation awards, and partner with Equity Administration and Controllership to ensure accurate, timely accounting and booking. - Coordinate with Tax on downstream impacts without owning tax conclusions. - Partner with Financial Reporting and Internal Controls to strengthen controls, SOX/ICFR readiness, impairment monitoring, audit trails, tie-outs, and subsequent-event procedures. - Monitor emerging accounting standards and translate new guidance into policies, implementation plans, disclosures, reporting calendars, and scalable processes. - Participate in cross-functional initiatives involving accounting-policy implementation, operating-model changes, legal-entity matters, and systems or process improvements. - Develop pragmatic accounting policies, playbooks, decision frameworks, and automation that improve consistency, strengthen capability, preserve judgment, reflect economic substance, and escalate unresolved issues. You might thrive in this role if you: - Hold a CPA, CA, or equivalent accounting qualification, or bring comparable demonstrated technical-accounting expertise. - Bring 5+ years of progressive experience in technical accounting, accounting advisory, public accounting, corporate controllership, or complex financial reporting, with meaningful industry or transaction experience. - Demonstrate broad U.S. GAAP expertise across corporate accounting, financial instruments, consolidation, business combinations, equity-method investments, debt and equity securities, impairment, fair value, financial statement presentation, and complex ownership structures. - Apply relevant guidance across ASC 320, 321, 323 326, 350, 360, 470, 480, 718, 805, 810, 815, and 820; and other applicable guidance as the facts require. - Have developed or reviewed audit-ready technical memoranda, implemented conclusions in recurring operations, worked constructively with external auditors, and ground
